newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end lower as Wall St, dollar fall.
newsitem.headline: German shares end lower as Wall St, dollar fall.

text.p: Germany's IBIS DAX index fell over two percent in late afternoon trade as the Dow Jones Industrial index on Wall Street stumbled ahead of the weekend, but German shares pulled back some losses later on.

There was much evidence of profit-taking both on the DAX and the Dow Jones as U.S. tech stocks were hit by disppointing earnings. Dealers said the German index seemed set to remain under pressure in the near-term.
The IBIS DAX ended the day down 71.97 points, or 1.71 percent at 4,131.94 points. Earlier the 30-share DAX index ended down 30.78 at 4,196.53 points.
Despite the losses, the DAX rose about four percent over the week, rising about 156 points from last Friday's close.
"I think the market looks a bit tired," said one dealer.
They said the losses would be constructive for the market to post further gains and reach new record levels.
Some of Friday's losses were tied to the expiry of the DAX options amid signs of heavy open interest at 4,200 points.
Overnight losses on Wall Street and losses in German debt markets, worried about the possible risk of a Bundesbank rate hike to help the mark, also capped market interest.
The market showed little reaction to the June Ifo business climate index report for west Germany, which rose beyond market expectations in June to 96.0 from a revised 95.4 in May.
Despite the general downward trend, banking stocks were in the focus after Commerzbank AG predicted many banks will report double-digit growth in first-half operating profit.
The report also said banking shares may also get a boost from speculation for mergers in the industry due to recent consolidation in the insurance sector.
Deutsche Bank AG which will report results on July 23, reached a new record high in bourse trade at 109.20 marks. Profit taking later on meant the share ended down 70 pfennigs at 106.90 marks.
Bayerische Hypo rose 1.20 marks to 58 marks and Dresdner Bank AG rose 56 pfennigs to 75.26 marks.
But Commerzbank fell 60 pfennigs to 53.50 marks.

Retailer Karstadt AG, which had surged more than 100 marks this week on takeover speculation, slumped on Friday to end bourse trade down 24 marks at 670 marks and ended electronic trade down 26 marks at 667.

Other notable shares posting losses that outpaced the market were carmaker Volkswagen AG, which ended down 44.50 marks at 1,395.50 marks, and chemicals group Degussa AG, which fell 3.05 marks to 93.38 marks.
